- 2026-09-16T06:10:07.120Z — rule: **A suggestion carries the 2.2 trust numbers of the detector that produced it, names no cause and proposes no change; approval binds to the candidate hash and is refused once the evidence set moves.** — chose **2.3 contract, settled before code. (1) A SUGGESTION IS A LOSS ROW, never a fix: {candidate hash, signal, scope = one initiative, evidence ids, count, corpus cutoff, engine version, detector report version, trust}. It names no cause and proposes no change; the fix, its predicted gain, its falsifier and its budget belong to Phase 3. (2) TRUST TRAVELS WITH IT: a candidate can only come from a detector the 2.2 protocol marked TRUSTED, and it carries that verdict's numbers (precision, recall, judged n, protocol and verdict event ids) so a reader sees how often this signal is right without leaving the row. Today that is `corrections` alone. (3) THE HASH IS THE EVIDENCE: sha256 over canonical {version, signal, scope, sorted evidence ids} — not the cutoff, not prose, not a branch. New evidence means a new candidate; a rejected candidate stays suppressed until its evidence set changes, which is exactly when its hash does. (4) APPROVAL BINDS TO THE EXACT CANDIDATE: approve, reject and revert re-derive candidates from the current log and refuse when the hash is no longer derivable, naming the hash that replaced it. Revert is a new event that ends an approval; nothing is erased or rewritten. (5) SURFACES: `sofar suggest [slug|--all] --dry-run [--json]` derives and prints, writing nothing; persistence is always an explicit verb — `suggest record|approve|reject|revert <hash>`; `suggest list` shows every candidate with its full history. `sofar tune` stays detection-only. No MCP tool and no digest section: the operator asks for suggestions, they are never pushed into every session's context. (6) MINIMUM EVIDENCE 3 instances in scope — one correction is ordinary work, a cluster is a pattern — and at most 10 open candidates per initiative. (7) PROTECTED FLOOR: the set of things a suggestion may ever change is today EMPTY (a loss row changes nothing), and log integrity, session routing, standing constraints, evaluator integrity, permissions and release policy are never in it.
